basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Anno sexcentesimo vitae Noe, mense secundo, septimo decimo die mensis, rupti sunt omnes'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Anno sexcentesimo vitae Noe, mense secundo, septimo decimo die mensis, rupti sunt omnes fontes abyssi magnae, et cataractae coeli apertae sunt, et facta est pluvia super terram quadraginta diebus et quadraginta noctibus. Menses apud Hebraeos non nisi juxta lunae cursum a prima usque ad primam computantur, primusque eorum mensis in quo pascha fieri praeceptum est, et in quo mundus est factus, appellatur Nisan, quem nos Aprilem vocamus. Secundus Jair, quem nos Maium dicimus, cujus die septimo decimo, id est, cum luna ejusdem mensis esset septima decima, venit diluvium, cum eodem ipso die intrasset Noe in arcam cum hominibus et animantibus cunctis ac volatilibus, quae per illam erant salvanda, hoc est enim quod sequitur.
